name: W-phase moment magnitude
description: Moment magnitude from inversion of the long-period W-phase (arrives between P and S waves); the USGS standard for larger global events

name: Centroid moment magnitude
description: Moment magnitude from a centroid moment tensor inversion of long-period surface waves

name: Body-wave moment magnitude
description: Moment magnitude from inversion of long-period body waves (P and SH)

name: Regional moment magnitude
description: Moment magnitude from inversion of complete waveforms at regional distances; common for moderate events in well-instrumented regions

name: Moment magnitude
description: Generic moment magnitude, based on seismic moment (rupture area × slip × rigidity); used when the specific method isn't labeled

name: Surface-wave magnitude
description: Based on the amplitude of Rayleigh surface waves with ~20-second periods

name: Short-period body-wave magnitude
description: Based on the amplitude of the first few cycles of the P wave (period ~1 s); saturates around 6.5

name: Lg-wave magnitude
description: Short-period magnitude based on the Lg surface wave; used mainly in central and eastern North America (also seen as MLg)

name: Local (Richter) magnitude
description: Original Richter scale: maximum amplitude on a horizontal seismograph, calibrated per region; the most common type for small local quakes

name: Duration magnitude
description: Based on the duration of shaking (coda length) at a station; common for small events in volcanic and California networks

name: Integrated P-wave magnitude
description: Moment magnitude estimated quickly from integrating the P waveform; used for rapid tsunami warning

name: Energy magnitude
description: Based on the radiated seismic energy rather than the moment; reflects how much shaking potential a quake has

name: Hand/non-standard magnitude
description: Magnitude assigned manually or by a non-standard method, often for historical or special-case events

name: Felt-area magnitude
description: Estimated from the size of the area where shaking was felt; used for historical events without instrumental data

name: Intensity magnitude
description: Estimated from observed shaking intensity reports; used mostly for historical events
